newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHIPPING COMPANY IN Q1 CONSOLIDATED PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: SHIPPING COMPANY IN Q1 CONSOLIDATED PROFIT.

text.p: The Latvian Shipping Company said on Monday that it posted a first quarter consolidated profit of $3.39 million against a planned loss of $5.5 million.
The company's turnover in the first quarter was $72.0 million and its profit from its shipping operations was $7.99 million, the company said in a statement.

Intensive work with bad debts as well as a better than planned performance by its refridgerated and tanker fleets were the reasons behind the first quarter profit, Andris Klavinsh, the company's president, told a news conference.
"The first quarter was not bad and we registered a profit of $4.79 million from our main business activity, operating ships," Klavinsh said.

Latvian Shipping, which has budgeted for a $20 million 1997 consolidated loss, said it hoped to revise its forecast upwards at the beginning of August, if the half year result shows an extended upward trend, Druvis Skulte, the company's board chairman, said.
"It has to be stressed, however, we will definitely not increase the expenditure side," Skulte said.
Latvian Shipping is estimated to be the world's 19th largest shipping firm and has 40 tankers, 24 reefers (refrigerated vessels) and seven dry cargo vessels.
In shipping operations, reefers and tankers have shown a slight turnover growth, while the dry cargo fleet has shown lower than planned results, Kalninsh said.
"Despite a good first quarter, Latvian Shipping does not exclude the possibility of facing difficulties in the coming quarters of 1997," Klavinsh said.
"It could be connected to the planned restructuring of the dry cargo fleet, a fall in the reefer market in the second half of the year and planned ship repairs in the third quarter," he said.
Klavinsh said that the first quarter figures could increase the value of Latvian Shipping in the eyes of foreign investors interested in privatising the company.

Some 13 foreign companies, including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Nomura have expressed an interest in participating in the privatisation of the company, to be completed in 1997.
